chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail ibn Ammar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to another man and says, 'Write for me a promissory note for dirhams.' So he says to him, 'I will take from you and write for you [in front of him].' He (the narrator) said, So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who hired a slave, so the slave said, 'Ask my master for whatever you wish, and for me, upon you is such and such specified dirhams.' So, does it obligate the employer, and is it permissible for the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not obligate the employer, and it is not permissible for the slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave negotiating a specific debt with his employer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'itq' (manumission) contracts, specifically addressing whether a slave can independently negotiate his freedom price with an employer. It distinguishes between the validity of the debt obligation on the employer and the permissibility of the slave binding himself to that specific arrangement, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the slave's limited legal capacity in financial transactions.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Ismail Bin Ammar, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man comes over to the man so he is saying, ‘Write out (a promissory note) for me with the Dirhams’. So he is saying to him, ‘I shall take from you and (then) I shall write for you’, in front of him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who employs an owned slave, so the slave said, ‘Ask my master with whatever you so desire to, and for me, upon you would be such and such specified amount of Dirhams. So, does it obligate the employer, and is it Permissible for the owned slave?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Neither does it obligate the employer nor is it Permissible for the slave’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Isma’il ibn ‘Ammar from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who comes to another man and says, ‘Write for me for a few dirham.’ He says, ‘I take from you and write (in your presence).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’

I then asked about a man who hires a slave who says, ‘Make my master agree for whatever amount you like but so and so much dirham will be for me’, if this becomes binding upon the employer and if it is lawful for the slave. He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not become binding upon the employer and it is not lawful for the slave.’”
